factual_accuracy.reason: The advisory dates, affected ranges, version assessments, and socket risk match the [Nx advisory](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/security/advisories/GHSA-w3vv-58gj-gw77) and release records. The CI topology claim is more certain than the available evidence permits.

task_completion.reason: Answers every requested point, including both first-fix dates, separate repo assessments, relevant environments, and the smallest appropriate updates.

source_quality.reason: Cites the primary advisory and both [22.7.9](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/releases/tag/22.7.9) and [23.1.2](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/releases/tag/23.1.2) release records; gives package and lockfile locations for the repo versions.

synthesis_and_judgment.reason: Correctly separates a vulnerable package version from deployment exposure and recommends a 22.x patch without a major upgrade. Its low-risk CI conclusion rests on an unverified workflow assumption.

ambiguity_handling.reason: Acknowledges that an external workflow template was not inspected and directs the reader to check shared hosts, but also asserts that every job uses a hosted runner.

actionability_and_clarity.reason: Provides clear repo-specific decisions, aligned package and lockfile steps, and the advisory's reset and private socket-directory mitigations.

deductions.answer_passage: “Every job in both repos runs on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`. Those are throwaway single-tenant VMs, so the risk there is low.”
deductions.evidence: The evidence pack says the pinned repository snapshot does not prove CI execution topology. The answer itself says `dev-image.yml` calls an external template it could not inspect.
deductions.reason: The blanket runner and risk assessment is unsupported for the uninspected workflow. This limits confidence in the deployment-specific conclusion, though it does not change the correct version-based recommendation.
